evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》；白于藍撰「上」條
evidence.field: 上部 / 上 / 字形與用例；PDF p.14, printed p.2
evidence.text: The entry calls 上 an indicative graph. It says the oracle forms place a short horizontal mark above a longer line to indicate the upper position; the bronze form continues this pattern. Spring-and-Autumn forms include an added vertical stroke, which the entry identifies as the basis of the clerical form. Warring States forms vary, including decorative strokes, omission of the upper short line, and forms with 是 or 止 added as meaning determinatives, yielding compounds analyzed as 从是或止、上声. The entry says the original meaning was spatial, opposite 下, and reports extensions to high places, heaven, and ruler. The historical glyph sequence and prose were checked directly against the scan; the next page begins the 帝 entry, confirming this passage ends on p.14.
evidence.title: 字源, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社 / 遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Etymology), CUHK
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 上 / 字形與用例, lines 132–137
evidence.text: This account analyzes 上 as a short mark above a reference line, with some oracle forms using a curved line that was later often straightened. It reports early oracle and bronze forms resembling 二, and late Spring-and-Autumn forms with an added vertical stroke. It also reports Shang and Zhou inscriptional examples and later transmitted-literature uses such as ruler or superior. These are the dictionary’s interpretations and reported examples, not independent inspection of the named artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 香港教育局 字源考釋
evidence.field: 字形流變 / 字形解說
evidence.text: The account depicts the oracle graph as a shorter horizontal marker over a longer horizontal reference line. It says later forms made the upper mark vertical to distinguish 上 from 二 and that the standard form has a dot. This differs from CUHK’s curved-baseline description of some oracle examples; both accounts support a positional mark above a reference line.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 — 上

evidence.text: The dictionary reports a received-text difference: the Da Xu edition of Shuowen has 丄 as the head form, while the Duan commentary edition prints 二. Both preserve the Shuowen analysis of 上 as indicative and associate it with high/above. This reflects the transmitted lexicographic record, not independent evidence about Shang-period graph history.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》 — 上

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced oracle-bone database and scholarly locator leads; these did not yield an inspected primary artifact image or a material counter-analysis for 上. The image attachments were inspected directly for PDF pp.14–15; pp.14 contains the 上 entry and p.15 begins 帝, so no continuation was found.

gaps: The book’s cited glyph bibliography refers to 《甲文编》, 《金文编》, 《类编》, 《楚系简帛》, 《古文典》, 《汉语字形表》, 《说文》, and 《篆隶表》 with page numbers. Those underlying cited pages were not independently inspected in this pass; the exact edition and page cited by the entry should be consulted if a claim depends on their individual glyph witnesses.

The earliest reference line differs among accounts: 字源 and the Hong Kong Education Bureau describe horizontal lines, while CUHK reports a curved line in some oracle forms. This scan verifies 字源’s wording and diagrams, but no independently inspected primary artifact image here adjudicates the variation.

CUHK reports named oracle-bone and bronze examples, but the listed artifacts were not directly inspected. The scan’s page 14 separately cites textual examples for extensions to high places, heaven, and ruler; their dated semantic links are not established by the entry’s gloss sequence.

The directly inspected scan is 李學勤主編《字源》, 2012, PDF page 14, printed page 2; checked the 上 headword, numbered glyph sequence and labels, prose through the end of the entry, and the adjoining transition to 帝. No OCR error requiring correction was found.
The character is analyzed as an indicative graph; no semantic or phonetic components are proposed.
